text: RPO and RTO are the two numbers that drive every HA/DR decision. RPO is how much data you're willing to lose. RTO is how long you can be down. Neither is a technology — they're business statements about acceptable pain, decided before anyone picks a tool.

The process runs business-first: ask what data loss and downtime the business can tolerate, write those answers down as real numbers, and only then choose a mechanism capable of hitting them. Picking the technology first is backwards.
Take a real requirement — "can't lose more than a few minutes, back within 30 minutes" — and it converts directly: RPO of 5 minutes, RTO of 30 minutes. That RPO rules out nightly-only backups.
Your RPO can never be tighter than your log backup frequency — Chapter 13's backup strategy feeds directly into this calculation. Next up: Always On Availability Groups.
